subject: Edge fallback orchestration & hosting tradeoffs — MAP and close cadence
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam@atlas.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlas.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: evaluation & MAP — hosting questions and timing

Marcus — thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement asked me to capture a few clarifying points before we finalize the MAP: 1) For production we need to pick a hosting lane (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Atlas has latency-sensitive inference (sub-200ms p95) for our customer-facing summarization flow; if we choose Hosted we need a clear SLA and regional residency (US East). 2) If we go Dedicated, what is the typical commit lead time and can Redwood provide an uplifted SLO for warm KV caching during rollouts? 3) We also need to understand the fallback orchestration: if Dedicated capacity drops, can traffic automatically route to Hosted with token-level cost visibility?

We want to land the MAP and SOW this week (target close: 2027-07-02). I attached the draft MAP and SOW. Can you confirm whether the MAP you shared supports a staggered canary (hosted -> dedicated) with a mid-rollover test window?

—Sam
[Attachment: Atlas_MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: Atlas_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam@atlas.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: evaluation & MAP — hosting questions and timing

Sam — thanks, and great notes. Short answers up front: 1) Hosted can meet sub-200ms p95 in US East for 8–12 token-window workflows if you adopt prefix KV caching and the streaming path; we’ll add a performance SLO to the MAP. 2) Dedicated lead time depends on pool availability and GPU flavor — typical procurement-to-live is 4–6 weeks for committed capacity; we can offer a burst-to-hosted fallback while Dedicated capacity ramps. 3) Yes: Smart routing supports automated fallback to Hosted with path-level token cost breakdowns surfaced in the Console.

I’ve sketched an explicit canary cadence in the MAP (see attached excerpt):
- Week 0: Contract signature + required security docs (SOC2 evidence, KMS agreement)
- Week 1–2: Staging validation in Atlas test VPC (private endpoints if requested)
- Week 3: Canary (10% on Dedicated, 90% Hosted) — monitor accuracy regressions, latency, and token cost
- Week 4: Ramp Dedicated to 50% if SLAs met, else rollback to Hosted and extend canary
- Week 6: Full cutover and retrospective

I’ll upload a short runbook and a DocuSign-ready SOW with the SLA clauses called out. Karthik — can you confirm Dedicated SKU lead times if the customer prefers A100-ish reservation? Laura — can you prepare the MAP with the SLA table filled? Vanessa — loop in Marketplace ops if they want a listing or procurement pathway.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: excerpt from MAP]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sam Carter <sam@atlas.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: evaluation & MAP — hosting questions and timing

Sam / Marcus — quick capacity clarification. If Atlas wants A100-equivalent reserved Dedicated, lead time is closer to 6 weeks for a firm reservation (we’ll need a minimal committed monthly spend). If the customer is flexible on GPU class (e.g., 80-bit quantized T4 family for lower unit cost) we can typically spin a Dedicated pool in ~3 weeks. For the warm KV caching: Dedicated supports sticky cache partitions; we can preserve prefix caches during rollouts but recommend a 48–72 hour warm window for heavy traffic.

If Atlas needs data residency (US East) and managed KMS, we can enable a private deployment variant, but that introduces an extra procurement step and usually shifts cutover to 8–10 weeks.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Carter <sam@atlas.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlas.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: evaluation & MAP — hosting questions and timing

Appreciate the detail. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and security: 1) Procurement wants clear milestones tied to invoicing (we prefer milestone billing at signature, canary success, full cutover). 2) Security wants SOC2 evidence and the option to require customer-managed KMS in Transit/At-Rest if we go Private. 3) We need a canonical fallback decision tree in the MAP so our ops team knows when to failover to Hosted (and who is the escalation owner at Redwood).

Targeting to sign on 2027-07-02; procurement will escalate to finalize commercial terms if we can map milestones and DocuSign link. Can you drop the revised MAP and an updated SOW with milestone billing?

—Sam

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam@atlas.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, aws-marketplace@amazon.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: evaluation & MAP — hosting questions and timing

Sam — attaching updated MAP (milestone rows filled) and an SLA clause summary; included a compact fallback decision tree in the "Operational Runbook" tab and an escalation contact list. Key changes: 1) Billing milestones: Signature (10%), Canary success (40%), Full cutover (50%) — configurable. 2) Canary policy: automatic rollback threshold = >1% drop in top-line accuracy OR >25% p95 latency regression for 30m window. 3) Fallback orchestration: Redwood will provision smart routing from Dedicated to Hosted during capacity shortfall; ops escalation path: on-call infra (Redwood) -> account team (Marcus) -> Atlas ops. 4) Private option: added optional KMS checkbox and estimated 8–10 week procurement runway.

DocuSign envelope created and linked here: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/12345. HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-3421.

If this aligns we can mark the MAP as final and Marcus will circulate the SOW for signature. Marcus — please confirm preferred dates for canary and handover slots next week.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
